newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade "bars" Zhirinovsky from entering Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade "bars" Zhirinovsky from entering Bosnia.

text.p: Yugoslav authorities have stopped Russian right-wing politician Vladimir Zhirinovsky from crossing into Bosnian Serb territory to address political rallies, a Yugoslav opposition party said on Monday.
The right-wing nationalist Serbian Radical Party (SRS) reported in a faxed statement that Yugoslavia had barred Zhirinovsky from entering Bosnia via the main crossing point at Sremska Raca.
Zhirinovsky had been invited by SRS leader Vojislav Seselj to address local Serbs at rallies in the towns of Brcko and Banja Luka, in northern Bosnia.

The SRS statement said Zhirinovsky had entered Yugoslavia on a Russian diplomatic passport earlier on Monday and had passed through the normal passport and customs controls before heading for the border.
A spokesman for the Serbian interior ministry said he had no information on the reported ban, or of any problems at the border. The Russian embassy declined to comment.

Seselj, who met Zhirinovsky on his arrival, condemned Belgrade's decision announced earlier on Monday to establish full diplomatic relations with Croatia, with which rump Yugoslavia fought a war in 1991.
Seselj, speaking to journalists, described the recognition of Croatia as a criminal act and a betrayal.

Zhirinovsky attacked the U.S. for seeking to dictate who could or could not stand in elections in Bosnia next weekend. Under the U.S.-brokered Dayton peace agreement indicted war criminals, such as former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic, are barred from running.

"Where do they get the right to order Karadzic whether he will take part or not?" Zhirinovsky told journalists, and attacked U.S. President Bill Clinton as having "a sick mind, one minute he is bombarding Baghdad and the other telling Belgrade what to do".
